newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli jets strike guerrilla targets in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli jets strike guerrilla targets in Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli fighter planes launched a series of air attacks against Palestinian and Lebanese guerrilla targets on Tuesday, wounding three guerrillas and a civilian, security sources said.

The jets knocked out a Hizbollah radio transmission antenna in Syrian-policed Bekaa Valley in eastern Lebanon, security sources said. A shepherd in the area was injured by flying debris from the exploding rockets, they said.

Israeli planes also fired rockets in two air attacks hours apart into a base of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine-General Command (PFLP-GC) in Sultan Yaqoub area in southeastern Lebanon, security sources said.
The sources said three PFLP-GC guerrillas, including the area commander, were wounded when the rockets hit concrete rooms at the base, 10 km (six miles) west of the border with Syria.

A PFLP-GC official said Israeli jets also fired rockets into the seaside Na'ameh hills south of Beirut where the group has bases. There was no immediate confirmation from independent sources of the raid.
PFLP-GC is a Damascus-based Palestinian group that is opposed to peace talks with Israel. It believes Palestine could be regained through armed struggle.

Tuesday's air raids came two days after seven Israeli soldiers were wounded in a clash with Hizbollah fighters in a border zone Israel occupies in south Lebanon. Israeli jets hit guerrilla-held areas bordering the zone immediately after the Sunday clash but no one was hurt.

In their first attack on the Bekaa Valley in six months, Israeli planes fired two rockets into a hill overlooking the town of Baalbek where the transmission antenna of the pro-Iranian group's Voice of the Oppressed radio station is situated.
Security sources said the radio went off the air after the antenna was hit. The rockets destroyed a room used by guards and an electric generator and flying debris wounded a shepherd.

Hizbollah's Bekaa official Mohammad Yaghi said the Baalbek raid was a breach of a U.S.-brokered ceasefire agreement that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon last April and which bars the targeting of civilian areas. Some 200 people, mostly civilians, were killed in the blitz aimed against Hizbollah.
Baalbek is a bastion for the Shi'ite Moslem group in the Bekaa Valley. The town is 70 km (44 miles) east of Beirut and 15 km (nine miles) west of the Lebanon-Syria border.
Hizbollah (Party of God) leads a guerrilla war on 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 allied local militia holding the border zone in south Lebanon to ward off attacks on northern Israel.

"We will step up our attacks (against Israeli forces in south Lebanon)...Let them (Israeli forces) know that we are able and that the struggle with them will continue until we kick them out of our land," Yaghi said.

In northern Israel on Tuesday, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said it would be impossible for Israel to forge peace with Syria unless Damascus, the main power broker in Lebanon, reined in Hizbollah guerrillas.
Visiting an Israeli army base on the Lebanese border, Netanyahu said it "would not be wise" for any side to set conditions for the resumption of Israeli-Syrian peace talks.

"But it is clear that for negotiations between Israel and Syria to make progress there must be direct and determined Syrian action to reduce terror here," he said, referring to Hizbollah attacks in Israel's occupation zone in Lebanon.
"It is impossible to advance peace between Israel and Syria if an indirect war against Israel is being waged here," Netanyahu said.
Tuesday's raids brought to at least 16 the number of Israeli air attacks into Lebanon this year.
